_comment: Target list for the LEARNING-focused Repo Radar rotation.
but a separate roster: this one scans for how other systems CLOSE their
learning loop, not for general agent frameworks.
Use it with the explicit flag:
Selection is index = floor(unixHours) % repos.length, so entries are
append-only to keep existing hour mappings stable.
Chosen against HUQAN's measured learning-loop gaps:
G1 experience chain is NOT_YET_WIRED (no production caller)
G2 dream hypotheses never promote to a Procedure Registry
G3 belief-revision contradiction does not feed learning
G4 no memory consolidation / forgetting / decay
G5 no calibration surface, so 'intelligence improved' is unprovable
Entries must be public repositories, live in 2026, and carry a real
license (verified via the GitHub API at curation time). 2024-stalled
repos were deliberately dropped: a stalled loop is a weak teacher.

repos.why: Darwin Godel Machine: the canonical open implementation of an archive-based self-improvement loop that keeps only changes that measurably improve a benchmark. Closes G2/G5 by showing how a hypothesis is promoted on evidence rather than on plausibility.
Batteries-included agent harness whose design decisions are driven by an end-to-end eval set. The most direct 2026 answer to G5: how a harness decides which middleware/prompt parts earn their place.
Encodes standard operating procedures as agent roles and handoffs. A source for G1: turning a successful run into a reusable, named procedure instead of a one-off trace.

AIDE: an outer loop that rewrites an inner research agent and scores each rewrite. Shows the propose-evaluate-accept structure HUQAN needs to promote a dream hypothesis into a compiled procedure (G2).
A memory OS that treats add/update/delete as scheduled decisions rather than passive writes. Targets G4 directly, where HUQAN only has tombstone/supersede and no consolidation or decay.
Instrumented execution where every action is a labelled step against a real task. A concrete source for G1: distilling a run into an experience record that a later request can reuse.
A serious eval framework with composable scorers and logging. Supplies the measurement surface for G5 so any 'intelligence increased' claim is backed by a repeatable score rather than an anecdote.
The reference harness for reproducible model scoring. Relevant to G5 for its task-registry and determinism discipline, which is what makes a benchmark comparable over time.
Eval + adversarial testing in one CLI with declarative assertions. A model for G5 that also touches guardrails: it treats a failed assertion as a first-class, regression-tracked signal.
Metric-centric evaluation that plugs into CI. Useful for G5 to see how a fuzzy, LLM-judged metric is made deterministic enough to gate a change.
Metrics for retrieval and faithfulness with synthetic test generation. Targets G4/G5: how to score whether recalled memory is actually correct, not merely present.
The eval runner behind Terminal-Bench, used to benchmark long-horizon agent tasks. A 2026-current model for G5: scoring an agent on end-to-end tasks instead of unit assertions.
The reference library for continual learning and the forgetting/replay strategies that fight it. Directly informs G4: consolidation without destabilising what was already learned.
A world model that learns from imagined rollouts. Relevant to HUQAN's dream loop (G2): how a simulator is kept honest so imagined experience does not poison real learning.
Optimises prompts and code by propagating natural-language critique. A different shape for the G2 promotion loop: candidate -> critique -> revised candidate, scored at each step.
Agent-driven prompt optimisation with explicit compression and demo-selection stages. Targets G1: learning a better prompt from past runs and measuring the gain before adopting it.
Solves geometry by deduction plus a learned search heuristic, emitting a proof trace. Relevant to HUQAN's inference layer: how derived conclusions carry an auditable justification chain.

A high-performance Datalog engine with stratified negation and provenance. The reference for G3: how retracting a fact correctly retracts everything derived from it, which HUQAN's semi-naive join does not yet expose.
A reasoning engine that explains why a conclusion holds. Supplies the justification/provenance pattern HUQAN needs when a belief revision must be attributable (G3).
Logical-form-guided reasoning over a knowledge graph with mutual indexing. A current example of grounding LLM reasoning in a graph so contradictions surface as structure, not as prompt drift (G3/G4).
A mature RDF framework with named-graph isolation and rule-based inference. A reference for G4: graph-level integrity and provenance accounting that survives concurrent writes.
A compact SPARQL database with a clear persistence and query model. Useful as a contrast for HUQAN's own graph store on durability and query planning boundaries.
The widely-used Python RDF toolkit, strong on graph algebra and serialization. A reference for graph mutation semantics and round-trip fidelity (G4).
A vulnerability scanner that probes an LLM with a structured attack taxonomy. Relevant to HUQAN's fail-closed gates: how a guardrail is proven to hold under adversarial input, not just happy paths.
Pairs agents with graph workflows that support type-safe routing, checkpointing and HITL. A current model for G1/G2: durable, resumable state is the substrate a learning loop needs.
Tree-of-Thought search over candidate reasoning paths. Relevant to G2: exploring several hypotheses and keeping the branch that verifies, instead of committing to the first plausible one.
